parole.testo: Given begadkefat, from Aramaic תותא / ܬܘܬܐ (tūṯā), from Iranian. See Persian توت (tut) for more.

parole.significato: rat (without any qualifying adjective sensu strictu referring to Rattus gen. et spp. and Meriones gen. et spp.)
parole.testo: From the root ج ر د (j r d) related to gnawing the exterior off, a variation like in the also common جِذْر (jiḏr, “root”) from ج د ر (j d r). In dialects also جُرْذ (jurḏ), and جُرْد (jurd), but a stop for this spirant is common in dialects. It finds cognates in Mehri gərḏīn (“rat”), Harsusi gerḏīn

Borrowed from Aramaic דּוּרְדָּא / דֻּרְדָּא (durdā), its plural דּוּרְדֵּי / דֻּרְדֵּי (durdī), an Iranian loanword, represented by Persian درد (dord, “dregs”). For this ending in Aramaisms, compare نُمِّيّ (nummiyy), نُوتِيّ (nūtiyy), سَكِّيّ (sakkiyy).

Borrowed from Aramaic סַרְגָא (sargā) (in Classical Syriac ܣܰܪܓܳܐ), from סְרַג (srag, “to bind, to plait”) (in Classical Syriac ܣܪܰܓ). A theory diffused by Abaev derives the word from Iranian, compare Sogdian [script needed] (sʾγr /⁠sāγr⁠/), Ossetian саргъ (sarǧ), but the Iranic words are, if relate
